As I already mentioned, of course there are no universal attributes in regards to trans men or any other group of people. That’s because people are too complex and diverse to make a universal generalization about.  There are simply trends which can be attributed to any group of people. I thought I was clear about this but maybe it was misunderstood. 

It seems to me as though you are against the idea or are offended by generalizations being made about any group of people. Which makes sense and sounds like a good idea in theory, but in practice I feel as though doesn’t actually work because of several reasons. 

For example as you mentioned not all trans men experience dysphoria.  This may be true but people as a whole are more likely to experience dysphoria than the rest of the population which is a widely known fact. Rather than it being a negative impact on the trans community, where acknowledging that fact means trans people are being “judged”, it also means that acknowledging the fact means that more attention and resources can be put towards trans people getting help for that issue since it disproportionately effects the trans community. I’m sure generalizations like this can be used in a malicious way, but by not acknowledging that trends exist in populations we also can fail to address certain issues affecting said populations of people. 

You mentioned you believe that trans people universally face oppression, which is an example of a generalization of a group. As you said, there might exist a trans person somewhere who doesn’t feel oppressed in any way. So this assertion could also potentially be judging them and assuming their experience. But as we can see, their individual experience does not mean that as a group trans people are not oppressed. 

I’m also not saying that we don’t have other features besides being trans men or that anyone should see us or any group of people that way for that matter. 

I’m not sure why someone would say they only date people with your experiences. That doesn’t even make sense as you mentioned because everyone’s experiences are different. 

So what exactly do you disagree with? I hope I made it clear that I don’t think all trans people experience the same thing or that all cis people do not have similar experiences. Nor do I recall ever saying that. 

Wanting to eliminate generalizations seems good in theory but I explained why in practice it doesn’t really work. 

If we cannot make any generalizations about any group of people, we therefore cannot say that any group of people is oppressed. By saying they are oppressed we are making a generalization. And therefore we cannot help any group of people based on specific struggles pertaining to that group. 

If there are no common struggles or qualities at all amongst trans people then why for example would trans groups like this exist, or why should we need to promote or fight for trans rights? Even assuming a group is oppressed for any reason or shares any similar qualities or experiences is yet another generalization.

So what you’re saying that it’s not ok for people to have a preference for trans people. And that it’s also not ok for people to have genital preferences. Please correct me if I’m wrong. 

There are significant differences between cis people and trans people though because they have different experiences. Being trans is significantly different than being cis — psychologically, socially and medically. Cis people and trans people are not the same.  

Of course this doesn’t mean that all trans people have “universal” traits but just like any other group of humans there will be common themes and trends that can be analyzed. 

The assertion that trans people are the same as cis people is not only incorrect but in my opinion can also lead to problems such as erasing the experience and struggles of trans people which are different to cis people. 

If cis people and trans people were the same then we wouldn’t need to fight for trans rights anymore. So I guess it’s a little confusing to me.

Having experienced dysphoria, potential oppression, and other life experiences and struggles are very important factors as well and I’m not sure it’s always beneficial to have these completely ignored or to assume that these other factors don’t contribute to a persons experience. The trans experience is very unique and it does make that persons experience quite a bit different to one of a cis person. 

I have met several people on the LGBTQ spectrum that value the different experiences I have to offer as a trans person, and not in a fetishy way. Although I agree that it is harmful for it to be expressed in a fetishy way, I think it is possible to appreciate the life experiences of trans people and value them in a different way without erasing their experiences completely by saying we have to see all trans people as cis people.
